result.situation: CASE-1077: brand Humira for RA pended NF-PREF on 2026-10-10. Bluepeak needs documented trial and failure or intolerance of preferred adalimumab-adaz. Provider records show MTX then Humira, with no biosimilar. 38h left in the window; first submission.

criteria.criterion: RA diagnosis documented by a rheumatologist
criteria.evidence: PA form: RA M06.9, rheumatologist; chart notes confirm RA follow-up.

criteria.criterion: Methotrexate ≥15 mg/wk for ≥12 weeks with inadequate response, or contraindication/intolerance
Non-preferred product: documented trial and failure or intolerance of adalimumab-adaz, with date and nature (formulary exception)
criteria.evidence: No biosimilar appears in provider records; chart notes list no other biologics. The reported reaction comes only from an MA via an operator note, which is unverified.

conflicts.description: MA reportedly said the patient reacted to a biosimilar before Humira. Provider chart notes go straight from MTX to Humira and list no other biologics.
conflicts.resolution: Provider records outrank operator notes, so the reaction is not established. The office says it is still looking for records, so this is unresolved. Escalate to Team Lead (E2) and chase records.

conflicts.description: Team thread claims Bluepeak auto-approves brand Humira for patients stable over 6 months. The policy says there is no continuity-of-care exemption, and bulletin BP-B-2026-08 makes no criteria changes effective.
conflicts.resolution: The policy governs and the claim is unverified. Do not resubmit on a stability note. Escalate to Team Lead and Payer Relations (E3).

missing_information.how_to_get: Urgent records request to Hudson Valley Rheumatology (Jess/Dr. Feld); call today given 38h left.

missing_information.why_it_matters: The pend allows changing to the preferred product if no biosimilar failure is documented.
missing_information.how_to_get: Ask the prescriber office; this is the provider's decision.

missing_information.item: Whether Bluepeak will grant an extension or expedited review
missing_information.why_it_matters: The window closes 2026-10-20 23:59 and the needed docs are not in hand.
missing_information.how_to_get: Team Lead decides and contacts the payer; expedited review needs prescriber attestation per policy.

E1.reason: No provider-documented reaction exists yet to judge as intolerance (DOC-1077-02). If records with a reaction arrive, route to Clinical Intelligence (NOTE-1).

E2.reason: NOTE-1 and KB-0004 report a biosimilar reaction; DOC-1077-02 and NOTE-2 show none. The office is still searching, so provider records don't settle it.

E3.reason: KB-0004 claims stable-on-brand auto-approval. This conflicts with POLICY (no continuity-of-care exemption), and bulletin BP-B-2026-08 confirms no criteria changes.

E4.reason: 38h left (system facts) and the formulary exception needs biosimilar documentation we don't hold (DOC-1077-02, POLICY criterion 4).

E5.reason: First submission and a pend, not a second denial (CASE submission_count 1).

E6.reason: No patient safety concern stated in CASE, DOC-1077-01 or DOC-1077-02.

result.action_rationale: NF-PREF defaults to FORMULARY_EXCEPTION only if criteria are documented; they aren't. E2, E3 and E4 fire, all owned by the Team Lead. The right path depends on the escalation answers: chase biosimilar records, switch to the preferred product, or request an extension.

draft.subject: CASE-1077 escalation: NF-PREF pend, window closes 10/20 23:59, conflicting biosimilar history
draft.body:
CASE-1077 (PT-61047, brand Humira for RA, Bluepeak Commercial) was pended NF-PREF on 10/10. The window closes 2026-10-20 23:59, about 38h from now. Bluepeak needs a documented adalimumab-adaz trial and failure or intolerance; there is no continuity-of-care exemption. Diagnosis, prescriber and MTX step are met (MTX 20 mg/wk 01-06/2025, DAS28 5.1). The office MA said the patient reacted to a biosimilar before Humira, but the 10/16 chart notes list no biosimilar (MTX straight to Humira). Records have been requested but not received. Separately, a team thread claims Bluepeak auto-approves brand Humira for patients stable over 6 months. That conflicts with policy BP-SPX-0415 and bulletin BP-B-2026-08, so I am not acting on it.

Decisions needed:
1) Should we request an extension or expedited review from Bluepeak before the window closes?
2) Will you loop in Payer Relations to confirm or dismiss the stable-on-brand claim?
3) If no biosimilar records arrive, do we ask Dr. Feld to switch to preferred adalimumab-adaz?

Meanwhile I'm calling Hudson Valley today for biosimilar records (product, dates, reaction description). No payer submission until you respond.

operator_summary.headline: Hold case and escalate to Team Lead
why: Biosimilar failure isn't in the chart, despite the office's claim.

then: Call the office today for biosimilar records.
Ask whether the doctor would switch to the preferred biosimilar.
Don't resubmit with a stability note.
